standard.title: Welded Low Carbon Steel Cylinders Exceeding 5 Litre Water Capacity for Low Pressure Liquefiable Gas — Requirements for Inspection and Reconditioning of Used LPG Cylinders (First Revision)
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the mandatory requirements for the inspection, materials, procedures, physical testing, and final marking for the reconditioning of used low-carbon steel LPG cylinders (with a water capacity exceeding 5 litres) originally manufactured in accordance with IS 3196 (Part 1), as well as the criteria to declare used cylinders completely unserviceable.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the mandatory requirements for the inspection, materials, procedures, physical testing, and final marking for the reconditioning of used low-carbon steel LPG cylinders (with a water capacity exceeding 5 litres) originally manufactured in accordance with IS 3196 (Part 1), as well as the criteria to declare used cylinders completely unserviceable.

certification.description: Mandatory Certification under the Gas Cylinder Rules of the Government of India, in coordination with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). Facilities undertaking the reconditioning or hot repair of LPG cylinders must hold a valid BIS license under IS 13258, and all reconditioned cylinders must carry the physical ISI mark and the reconditioner's license number (CM/L) to certify safe return to active commercial rotation.
requirements: Any numerical value representing the result of a physical test or chemical analysis must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
If any loss in tare weight is observed under Clause 10.4 during reconditioning, the value of this loss must be permanently punched on the foot ring (e.g., LTW 200 to represent a loss of 200 g).

To visually identify the cylinder as a reconditioned unit, the letter 'R' must be conspicuously stamped on the vertical stay of the valve protecting ring as close to the certification mark as practicable.

Reconditioned cylinders must comply with their original design criteria, verifying physical parameters such as maximum working pressure (MPa), hydrostatic test pressure (MPa), and water capacity (litres).

Under the active Amendment No. 1 (March 2021), the preparation of the reconditioned cylinder for dispatch (including capping, valving, and thread protection) must conform strictly to Clause 23 of IS 3196 (Part 1).
Establishes strict visual, physical, and thickness limits during inspection to declare a used LPG cylinder completely unserviceable (e.g., excessive corrosion, cuts, gouges, dents, or bulging).
Provides requirements for pneumatic testing, hydrostatic testing, and joint inspections after executing repairs or reconditioning on the cylinder shell.
